description: Reviewed downstream SDK alignment classifications, evidence associations, explanations, and related spec PR attribution.

reports.reason: Assessment and SDK changelogs identify the clusterName and result-model breaking changes. The SDK release also carries later changes, but the relevant findings align.
reports.rootCause: The assessed spec directly changed the private-endpoint operation and supporting models: clusterName became a required method input, the update method was replaced, and helper models were removed. The Python and Java breaks are generated consequences of that contract change.

reports.reason: Assessment and SDK changelogs identify the model and property breaks. The generated release also includes later #46924 changes to the same 2026-08-01-preview surface, including compliance-lock operations and role-assignment alignment. Both SDK PRs were closed without merging, so this is generated-surface evidence rather than shipped-package evidence.
reports.rootCause: The assessed spec directly renamed and removed model members, made response properties required, and replaced the CloudAccount update model. Later #46924 aligned the same preview version and contributed additional generated release content, but the assessed breaking items remain consequences of #46679.

reports.reason: Assessment reports the removal of the private-endpoint update method. Python and Java list the corresponding update rename or replacement. Additional delete-signature changes came from earlier #44288, while helper-model removals are grouped under the same root method change.
reports.rootCause: The assessed spec removed or replaced the private-endpoint update operation, producing the matching SDK method removal or rename. The shared SDK release also repeats older #44288 changes, but those are secondary to the directly matched operation change.

reports.reason: Assessment and Java align on tokenId becoming optional. Python reports the same change plus additional Python-specific TypedDict removals.
reports.rootCause: The assessed spec made tokenId optional, and both assessment and SDK evidence reflect that requiredness relaxation. Python TypedDict removals are additional Python generator cleanup, not the root of the matched break.

reports.reason: Python reports no breaking change. Java changes ResourceOperation from a class to an interface because the model becomes a paged-operation item, a Java Fluent-specific generation effect.
reports.rootCause: Paging-item generation changes Java ResourceOperation from a serializable model class to a Fluent interface and removes fromJson/toJson. Python and the neutral TCGC contract do not expose that Java-only representation.

reports.reason: Python lists no breaking change. Java's ResourceOperation class-to-interface break was triggered by earlier #44101. The #44524 assessment findings are C# customizations and an inferred error-model replacement, so they are not expected to appear consistently in Python or Java changelogs.
reports.rootCauseCategory: SDK release includes other spec changes
reports.rootCause: TCGC produced no downstream finding for #44524, while the Java breaking section repeats the ResourceOperation representation change triggered by earlier #44101. The mapped SDK release therefore contains a breaking change from another spec PR; the C#-specific #44524 findings are a separate language surface.

reports.outcome: Not aligned, but the difference is expected
reports.reason: The SDK breaking items were introduced by earlier spec changes. The SDK release aggregates multiple spec PRs, while assessment evaluates only #46008.
reports.rootCauseCategory: SDK release includes other spec changes
reports.rootCause: The SDK release breaking section reflects relationship-model changes introduced by earlier API-version PRs, especially #44941 and #45024. The PR-scoped assessment of #46008 does not contain those earlier changes.

reports.outcome: Not aligned, but the difference is expected
reports.reason: Python 4.0.0 explicitly links the listed method breaks to the operations migration and the model changes to hybrid-model migration. Java lists generated Fluent helper and overload removals. These changelog breaks are migration and generator effects rather than evidence that #43918 introduced a neutral downstream contract break.
reports.rootCause: Python 4.0.0 explicitly attributes method breaks to the TypeSpec operations migration and model reshaping to the hybrid-model migration. Java lists Fluent generator removals such as validate methods and convenience overloads; these are migration-generated language surface changes, not neutral REST or TCGC breaks introduced by #43918.

reports.reason: Assessment reports no downstream breaking changes, and neither SDK changelog lists a breaking change.
reports.rootCause: The assessed spec change is additive for the generated Python and Java surfaces. Neither assessment nor either mapped changelog identifies a downstream compatibility break.

reports.reason: Assessment reports no downstream breaking changes, and the SDK changelogs contain only additive operations and models.
reports.rootCause: The assessed operations and models are additive. The mapped Python and Java release entries contain no breaking section.

reports.reason: Neither assessment nor the available SDK changelogs report a breaking change. Java is an initial release, so historical comparison is limited, but the observed evidence is aligned.
reports.rootCause: The assessed change produces no neutral downstream break and the mapped Python release is additive. Java is an initial release, so it has no prior package baseline, but the available evidence contains no conflicting break.

reports.reason: Assessment reports no downstream break, but no Python or Java management SDK release could be mapped to API 2026-04-01. The visible SDK releases predate this spec PR.
reports.rootCause: No Python or Java management SDK release can be mapped to the assessed 2026-04-01 API. Without a target release entry, the assessment result cannot be compared to SDK changelog behavior.

reports.reason: The three assessment findings are C#-only ResourceIdentifier alternate types. No defensible Python or Java SDK release mapping was found for API 2026-06-01.
reports.rootCause: The assessment findings are C# ResourceIdentifier alternate-type changes, and no Python or Java release can be mapped to the assessed 2026-06-01 API. There is no comparable language release evidence.

reports.outcome: Not aligned, but the difference is expected
reports.reason: Python is additive. Java records broad removal of generated validate methods and update-wrapper helpers caused by the TypeSpec-generated SDK migration rather than a neutral contract break in this PR.
reports.rootCause: TCGC produced no downstream finding and Python is additive, while Java broadly removes generated validate methods and update-wrapper helpers. This repeated generator-surface pattern is attributable to the TypeSpec SDK migration, not to the assessed PR's neutral contract.

reports.reason: The assessment was blocked. Both SDK releases compare against an earlier package and aggregate intervening spec changes, so their breaking sections cannot be attributed to #44334 alone.
reports.rootCause: The historical assessment lacks a completed downstream result. The mapped SDK releases also aggregate intervening spec changes, so their breaking sections cannot be attributed to this PR while the assessment is blocked.

reports.reason: The current reassessment reports no downstream SDK breaking changes. Both emitted SDKs retain Encryption, add StorageAccountEncryption, and list no breaking changes.
reports.rootCause: The reassessed neutral SDK contract and both generated language changelogs agree: Encryption remains available, StorageAccountEncryption is additive, and there is no downstream breaking change.

reports.outcome: Not aligned, but the difference is expected
reports.reason: Python is additive. Every Java breaking item is a removed generated validate method from the TypeSpec-generated SDK migration; the assessed feature models and operations themselves are additions.
reports.rootCause: TCGC produced no downstream finding and the assessed API changes are additive, while Java removes only generated validate methods. The break is a TypeSpec SDK migration effect rather than a contract change introduced by this PR.

reports.outcome: Not aligned, but the difference is expected
reports.reason: TCGC reports that ManagedClusters.delete gains the optional ignore-pod-disruption-budget public parameter, changing the ordered language-neutral signature. Python and Java do not list this optional-parameter addition as breaking.
reports.rootCause: The neutral TCGC contract treats the added optional delete parameter as a positional-signature compatibility risk. The generated Python and Java surfaces handle the optional input without recording a changelog break, so the language-specific compatibility result differs from the neutral contract.

reports.reason: No defensible Python or Java management SDK release association was found for API 2026-07-01-preview.
reports.rootCause: No Python or Java management SDK release can be defensibly associated with the assessed 2026-07-01-preview API. Existing package releases target different API versions.

reports.outcome: Not aligned, but the difference is expected
reports.reason: Assessment identifies two removed response properties. Both SDK packages are initial releases, so no previous published SDK surface exists for the changelog to describe as breaking.
reports.rootCauseCategory: Initial SDK release has no comparison baseline
reports.rootCause: The assessment detects removals relative to the spec baseline, but both language packages are initial releases. With no previously published SDK surface, their changelogs cannot report a package-level breaking change.

reports.outcome: Not aligned, but the difference is expected
reports.reason: Python explicitly documents TypeSpec hybrid-model and operations migrations, while Java lists Fluent validation and representation changes. The mapped SDK breaks are dominated by TypeSpec migration rather than a neutral TCGC contract change.
reports.rootCause: Python explicitly identifies TypeSpec hybrid-model and operations migrations, including properties nesting and keyword-only method parameters. Java additionally changes Fluent validation and representation helpers; the dominant breaks are migration effects rather than a neutral TCGC delta in this PR.

reports.reason: Assessment and Python both record the ServiceGateways method renames caused by LRO generation. Java remains additive because its generated operation surface differs; #44613 broadens the release context but is not the primary cause.
reports.rootCause: The assessed LRO changes produce method renames in Python, while the Java generated surface remains additive. The mismatch is primarily language-specific operation generation; the earlier #44613 only broadens the release context.

reports.outcome: Not aligned, but the difference is expected
reports.reason: The shared SDK release includes later #46566 changes to the same 2026-08-01-preview version. Its required-property reordering removes three Java Fluent definition stages while Python reports no source break; those removals are not changes introduced by #45167.
reports.rootCauseCategory: SDK release includes other spec changes
reports.rootCause: Later #46566 reordered required StorageAppliance properties across API versions, including 2026-08-01-preview. Java Fluent translated that other spec PR into three definition-stage removals, while the assessed #45167 changes remain additive and Python reports no break.

reports.reason: The assessment was blocked. Both initial SDKs were generated after #45624 for a later API version, not for the assessed 2026-06-30-preview surface alone.
reports.rootCauseCategory: SDK targets a different API version
reports.rootCause: The assessment is blocked for 2026-06-30-preview, while both initial SDKs were generated after #45624 from 2026-09-01-preview. The SDK entries do not represent the assessed API surface.

reports.reason: The SDK PRs emit stable 2026-11-01 from aggregate parent #45288, while the assessment isolates a 2026-11-02-preview child fix. The SDK breaking sections cannot be attributed to #45348 alone.
reports.rootCauseCategory: SDK targets a different API version
reports.rootCause: The assessment isolates a 2026-11-02-preview child fix, but the SDK PRs emit stable 2026-11-01 from aggregate parent #45288. Their breaking sections describe a different, broader API input.

reports.reason: Both exact-API generated changelogs contain no breaking changes, matching the assessment. The SDK PRs are not both merged, so this is generated rather than fully shipped evidence.
reports.rootCause: Both SDKs were generated for the exact assessed API and contain no breaking section, matching the assessment. Publication state limits shipment evidence but does not create a contract mismatch.

reports.reason: The spec project has no Python or Java emitter configuration, no downstream package surface was found, and the assessment was blocked.
reports.rootCause: The TypeSpec project configures neither Python nor Java emitters and no language package surface exists. The blocked downstream assessment therefore has no SDK changelog counterpart.

reports.outcome: Not aligned, but the difference is expected
reports.reason: All ten assessment findings are C# client-name or alternate-type changes, so they are not expected in Python or Java. The SDK releases also aggregate other API-version and migration changes.
reports.rootCauseCategory: Assessment and SDK compare different language surfaces
reports.rootCause: The assessment findings are C# client-name and alternate-type customizations, while Python and Java changelogs describe their own return-type, wrapper, and API-version changes. The evidence compares different language surfaces and release scopes.

reports.outcome: Not aligned, but the difference is expected
reports.reason: The assessment finding concerns an LRO final-state GET destination. That is runtime polling behavior, not a public type or signature change normally listed in generated SDK changelogs.
reports.rootCause: The assessment finding changes the LRO final-state GET destination. That polling behavior can affect runtime semantics without changing the public methods or models normally enumerated in generated SDK changelogs.

reports.reason: Python confirms the hostname and scanDnsName removals found by the assessment. Java was generated after #46662 deliberately preserved those members, so no Java breaking changes remained.
reports.rootCause: The spec removal reaches Python and matches the assessment, but later #46662 adds Java-specific compatibility preservation before Java generation. Java therefore retains members that Python removes.

reports.reason: The PR only adds C# names intended to preserve .NET compatibility. Python and Java regeneration entries contain no breaking section.
reports.rootCause: The PR adds C# naming metadata to preserve .NET compatibility and does not change the neutral Python or Java surface. Both regeneration entries contain no breaking section.

reports.reason: Both SDKs are initial releases, but the assessment was blocked by unavailable compiler, AutoRest, and TCGC baselines. There is no assessed downstream result to compare.
reports.rootCause: Compiler, AutoRest, and TCGC baseline artifacts are unavailable, so no downstream assessment result exists. Initial SDK releases also have no prior package baseline for comparison.

reports.reason: Both changelogs contain additive capability models and properties only, matching the assessment's zero downstream-breaking findings. The release also includes later #46658, which renamed PrefixDefinition to PrefixConfiguration in the same 2026-10-01-preview version before SDK generation.
reports.rootCause: The assessed capability models and properties are additive. Later #46658 finalized the same-version model name as PrefixConfiguration, so the aggregated Python and Java changelogs list the combined surface as additions only.

reports.reason: The assessment was blocked, and neither SDK PR is merged or published. The exact generated mappings are provisional initial-release evidence only.
reports.rootCause: The historical assessment could not produce required downstream artifacts, and both SDK PRs remain provisional initial releases. There is neither a completed assessment nor a published prior SDK baseline.
